2028.title: 2028 United States presidential election
2028.lead:
A presidential election was held in the United States on November 7, 2028. The Democratic ticket of California junior senator Adam Schiff and Wisconsin citizen Christopher J. Jones-Wheel defeated the Republican ticket of former Florida governor Ron DeSantis and Connecticut activist Luca Jardine.

Incumbent Republican president Donald J. Trump was ineligible to run for a third term due to the term limits established by the Twenty-second Amendment to the United States Constitution. DeSantis nabbed the Republican nomination by March 2028, defeating his main challengers David Bruchey and Ted Cruz, and selected Luca Jardine as his running mate. The Democratic primaries were marked by a sharp contest between Schiff and the initial front-runner, former vice president and California senator Kamala Harris, who was the democratic nominee the previous presidential election. After a long primary season, Schiff narrowly secured the Democratic nomination in June 2028 and selected Christopher J. Jones-Wheel as his running mate.

During his second term in office, Trump's popularity declined significantly, which was attributed to the growing economic pains from the Iran War and the closing of the Strait of Hormuz. DeSantis opted to distance himself from Trump and did not campaign with him, nor did Trump appear in person at the 2028 Republican National Convention, although he did endorse DeSantis. Schiff strongly opposed the Iran War, as well as a troop surge and national draft that had begun in 2027, while DeSantis supported the war. Schiff campaigned on the theme that "Washington must change", while DeSantis emphasized his experience.

Schiff won a decisive victory over DeSantis, winning the Electoral College and popular vote by the largest margins since Republican Ronald Reagan in the 1984 United States presidential election, and flipping eight states that had voted Republican in 2024: Alaska, Arizona, Georgia, Michigan, Nevada, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin, as well as Nebraska's 2nd congressional district.

2032.title: 2032 United States presidential election
2032.lead:
A presidential election was held in the United States on November 2, 2032. Incumbent Democratic president Adam Schiff and his running mate, Incumbent vice president Christopher J. Jones-Wheel, were re-elected to a second term; they defeated the Republican ticket of Connecticut activist Luca Jardine and Maryland State Senator David Bruchey, and the Yellow Party ticket of former NFL wide receiver Garrett Wilson and Illinois journalist Jacob Camarda.

Schiff and Jones-Wheel were re-nominated by their party with no difficulty. Meanwhile, numerous Republican candidates entered the competitive primaries, with Jardine considered the early front runner. Jardine clinched the nomination in late August 2032 after defeating challenges by former Utah senator Mike Lee and House Minority Leader Ed Gallrein. Jardine selected David Bruchey as his running mate, a newly-elected State Senator from Maryland and the brother of Andrew Bruchey. Garrett Wilson ran as the Yellow Party candidate, although he was excluded from the presidential debates.

Adam Schiff was projected to win the Electoral College in a landslide once again, having secured 323 electoral votes last election. Schiff's first term was earmarked by the implementation of single-payer public healthcare to the United States, titled United States National Providers Association (USNPA), joining countries like Canada and the United Kingdom with universal free healthcare. Schiff negotiated several parts of the bill, using his congressional experience in the House of Representatives and Senate to appease all factions of Congress. USNPA was passed on March 6, 2030. Schiff is also credited with reforming the veterans aid system in the United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). Veterans disability fraud became a hot-button issue in the 2028 United States presidential election, as both parties made campaign promises to reform the system by which veterans are given aid. 

On election day, Schiff defeated Jardine by a wide margin, winning 383 electors to Jardine's 118 and taking 43.35% of the national popular vote to Jardine's 36.58%. The Yellow Party significantly outperformed polls and expectations by the media, winning 34 electors and a staggering 20.04% of the national popular vote. This was the largest Electoral College win and national popular vote win by a third party ever.

presidents.title: List of presidents of the United States
presidents.leadParagraph:
The president of the United States is the head of state and head of government of the United States, indirectly elected to a four-year term via the Electoral College. Under the U.S. Constitution, the officeholder leads the executive branch of the federal government and is the commander-in-chief of the United States Armed Forces.

The first president, George Washington, won a unanimous vote of the Electoral College. The incumbent president is Donald Trump, who assumed office on January 20, 2025. Since the office was established in 1789, 45 men have served in 47 presidencies. The discrepancy is due to the nonconsecutive terms of Grover Cleveland (counted as the 22nd and 24th president) and Donald Trump (counted as the 45th and 47th president).

vice-presidents.title: List of vice presidents of the United States
vice-presidents.lead: The vice president of the United States is the second-highest officer in the executive branch of the United States federal government, after the president of the United States. The vice president is also the president of the Senate. Vice presidents have exercised this latter power to varying extents over the years. There have been 50 vice presidents since the office was created in 1789. The incumbent vice president is Christopher Johnson Jones-Wheel, who assumed office as the 50th vice president on January 20, 2029.
